name: WE-047 Kestrany Sugar Import Regime Act (loop)

readings: U1-a: surrendered quantities return to the quota and are allocated again in the same year to registered importers on application
U1-b: surrender cancels the licence and the surrendered quantity lapses for that year

a1.text: At the old landed price (about $550 a tonne, white), demand for imports would exceed 400,000 t.

a2.text: Customs enforce the out-of-quota rate and licence limits.

a4.text: Foreign supply comes from many competing exporters, and no exporting country administers a share of the quota.

a10.text: Sugar can be imported ahead in 2026 at 25% and stored into 2027, and is expected to sell higher after January.

a19.text: Some licence volume is left unused and unsold on 30 September each year.

a20.text: Under U1-a, applications for surrendered quantities exceed them, and the Minister's rules allocate them otherwise than by price.

a27.text: The licence office's budget is raised with its task.

a32.text: The licence office's running cost exceeds the registration and transfer fees it receives.

j_reg.text: Every firm that imports sugar must register as an importer for $500.

j_fee.text: Transfers of shares and licences must be registered with the licence office for a $200 fee.

j_inc.text: Exporters can sell the sugar that Kestrany does not buy to other buyers in the world market.
